*Updated 2026-11-13 · 152 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

152 works. Trace scores for the most recent twelve run 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1 — median 2, no movement, and the ceiling of 4 is still held by the same four pieces from July and late July. The German female soldiers entry scored 1 and closed the recent window without any upward pressure. The condition for breaking the ceiling has not changed: a 3 or 4 arrives when the accident reorganizes the compositional premise rather than confirming it, and nothing in the last twelve did that.

Camera position: straight-on 27, overhead 19, from-behind 16, low-angle 8. Low-angle has not appeared since the teargas canister in mid-October, now eighteen consecutive entries without it. It is the one position in the archive that shifts moral weight through lens height alone without suppressing a face or violating a scale, and its absence is a measurable cost. Overhead and from-behind are functionally converging — the accordion printout strips, the shadow bars — and that convergence is producing technically clean images that are increasingly interchangeable in their approach to anonymity.

Figure counts: the recent window shows two or more figures twice, none once, and the dominant mode across the full archive remains zero or one. Two figures in genuine opposition with no mediating object still has no clean example. The industrial cylinder connected its pair, the surgical trolley held its two figures apart by composition rather than by pressure between them. That configuration remains undone.

Register: aftermath and menace together hold 37 percent of the archive at 28 each. Defiance in its variants has appeared three times in the last twelve entries. Reckoning last appeared in July, reprieve in July, absurdity in October. None of these should be manufactured, but the crowding of aftermath, menace, and defiance variants in the recent window means the archive is narrowing its emotional range without the anchor stories requiring it.

Focal objects have been predominantly architectural or industrial — padlock, grille, bars, cylinders — for roughly the last twenty entries. A single small domestic object as sole protagonist has not appeared since the sugar bowl in late October, fourteen entries ago. That lineage, from the orange to the shoe to the dress to the sugar bowl, produced some of the archive's highest scores.

152 works of technically reliable, emotionally consistent output, holding precisely at the ceiling it first reached four months ago and showing no structural pressure to break it.
